<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915437_theRebbe_101" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915437_theRebbe_101__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Through engagement with Torah, one affects the world to become a vessel for G-dliness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And behold, through engaging in Torah, one also affects the world so that it becomes a vessel for G-dliness.</t>
    <t s="1">For through the Torah having traveled and descended etc. until it became clothed in physical matters so that a person can grasp it in his thought, speech, and action,</t>
    <t s="2">through this one also draws down into the world.</t>
    <t s="3">For it is known</t>
    <t s="4">that the Ten Utterances with which the world was created</t>
    <t s="5">correspond to the Ten Commandments,</t>
    <t s="6">as it is brought in the Zohar</t>
    <t s="7">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="8">"Ten, ten the shekel for the holy shekel,"</t>
    <t s="9">and therefore through engaging in Torah</t>
    <t s="10">(the Ten Commandments)</t>
    <t s="11">one affects the Ten Utterances,</t>
    <t s="12">so that they too will be in the holy shekel.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Ten Utterances and Ten Commandments are equivalent, each affecting the other, with man's service in the lower world impacting the higher realms.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that this—that the Ten Utterances and the Ten Commandments are equivalent one opposite the other—</t>
    <t s="2">the intention in this is also that each one affects the other.</t>
    <t s="3">For just as the Ten Commandments affect</t>
    <t s="4">(as above)</t>
    <t s="5">the Ten Utterances,</t>
    <t s="6">and as the statement,</t>
    <t s="7">"He looked into the Torah and created the world,"</t>
    <t s="8">that the creation of the world is through the Ten Utterances as they are in the Torah,</t>
    <t s="9">which later descended in the aspect of "ordinary speech"</t>
    <t s="10">to bring the world into existence,</t>
    <t s="11">so too is it conversely,</t>
    <t s="12">that man's service in the matters of the world, which was created through the Ten Utterances of "ordinary speech," affects the Ten Commandments</t>
    <t s="13">[therefore there is an interpretation</t>
    <t s="14">in the Zohar's statement on the verse "Ten, ten" etc.,</t>
    <t s="15">that the Ten Utterances are higher than the Ten Commandments].</t>
    <t s="16">And it can be said that this is according to what is explained in Iggeret HaKodesh,</t>
    <t s="17">that the clarification of a law in Torah is specifically through a soul in a body,</t>
    <t s="18">and therefore the supernal ones come to hear novel Torah insights from the lower ones</t>
    <t s="19">(and as our sages said</t>
    <t s="20">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="21">"Friends hearken to your voice").</t>
    <t s="22">And to the extent that the Holy One, blessed be He, says to the ministering angels, "What are you asking Me? I and you will go to the court below."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Similarly, through the service of the bridegroom and bride below, additional light is drawn into their supernal counterparts, even in their highest root before the tzimtzum.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And so too is it with a bridegroom and bride,</t>
    <t s="1">that despite the fact that the bridegroom and bride below are derived from the aspect of bridegroom and bride above,</t>
    <t s="2">whose concept in the Sefiros is Zeir Anpin and Malchus,</t>
    <t s="3">and higher still, the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah</t>
    <t s="4">(bridegroom and bride)</t>
    <t s="5">are the matter of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum and the line, as explained at length in the discourses of my master, the Rebbe Maharash,</t>
    <t s="6">to the extent that the concept of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is also before the tzimtzum,</t>
    <t s="7">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="8">specifically through the service below</t>
    <t s="9">(and in particular through the joy of the bridegroom and bride below)</t>
    <t s="10">they draw additional light into the bridegroom and bride above, even as they are in their first root before the tzimtzum.</t>
    <t s="11">And in the manner that specifically through engaging in Torah and mitzvos below, the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is effected,</t>
    <t s="12">as explained in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="13">even as they are supernal beyond supernal.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
